51011-the-ghost-camp-or-the-avengers.creator: Rolf Boldrewood
51011-the-ghost-camp-or-the-avengers.description: A book by Rolf Boldrewood. He was prepared for bush travelling—although his term of “colonial experience,” judging from his ruddy cheek and general get-up, had been limited. A rift in the over-hanging cloud-wrack, through which the low sunrays broke with a sudden gleam, showed a darksome mountain range to the south, with summit and sides, snow-clad and dazzling white.

65714-the-dance-of-life.title: The Dance Of Life
65714-the-dance-of-life.creator: Havelock Ellis

Bacon had in him the genius to create such a Renaissance three centuries earlier; there was no atmosphere for him to live in and he was stifled. But Malherbe, who worshipped Number and Measure as devoutly as Descartes, was born half a century before him.

arxiv-1804-06515.title: Faster Evaluation of Subtraction Games
arxiv-1804-06515.creator: David Eppstein
arxiv-1804-06515.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by David Eppstein. Subtraction games are played with one or more heaps of tokens, with players taking turns removing from a single heap a number of tokens belonging to a specified subtraction set ; the last player to move wins.

arxiv-2112-13422.title: A depleted and numerical model for pulsed Gaussian wave type II second harmonic generation
arxiv-2112-13422.creator: Mostafa Mohammad Rezaee, Mohammad Sabaeian, Alireza Motazedian, Fatemeh Sedaghat Jalil-Abadi
arxiv-2112-13422.description: Abstract This paper presents a three-dimensional (3-D) and spatio-temporal dependent nonlinear wave model to explain the generation of pulsed Gaussian Second Harmonic Waves (SHW). We solve numerically three coupled equations describing the type II Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) in cylindrical KTP crystals under the assumption of fundamental waves depletion, two for ordinary and one for extraordinary Fundamental Waves (FW).

arxiv-2212-03565.title: Essential Hereditary Undecidability Thanks: I thank Yong Cheng and Fedor Pakhomov for enlightening discussions. I am grateful to Fedor for his kind permission to use a proof-idea of his. I thank Taishi Kurahashi for his many suggestions for improvement of a previous version of this paper.
arxiv-2212-03565.creator: Albert Visser
arxiv-2212-03565.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Albert Visser. In this paper we study essential hereditary undecidability . Theories with this property are a convenient tool to prove undecidability of other theories. The paper develops the basic facts concerning essentially hereditary undecidability and provides salient examples, like a construction of essentially hereditarily undecidable theories due to Hanf and an example of a rather natural essentially hereditarily undecidable theory strictly below R . We discuss the (non-)interaction of essential hereditary undecidability with recursive boolean isomorphism.

arxiv-2306-07567.title: Large Language Models Sometimes Generate Purely Negatively-Reinforced Text
arxiv-2306-07567.creator: Fabien Roger
arxiv-2306-07567.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fabien Roger. When using adversarial training, it is common practice to train against the most egregious failures. However, this might imply using examples with sensitive information (such as leaked passwords or security vulnerabilities) as training data. One might assume that language models trained with gradient descent never generate text snippets which were only present in examples associated with the lowest possible reward. In this paper, we show that this assumption is wrong: in some situations, large language models do learn from such negatively-reinforced examples.

arxiv-2404-05520.title: The Fact Selection Problem in LLM-Based Program Repair
arxiv-2404-05520.creator: Nikhil Parasaram, Huijie Yan †, Boyu Yang †, Zineb Flahy, Abriele Qudsi, Damian Ziaber, Earl T. Barr, Sergey Mechtaev
arxiv-2404-05520.description: Abstract Recent research has shown that incorporating bug-related facts, such as stack traces and GitHub issues, into prompts enhances the bug-fixing capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Considering the ever-increasing context window of these models, a critical question arises: what and how many facts should be included in prompts to maximise the chance of correctly fixing bugs?

arxiv-2412-08175.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Model Collapse in Rectified Flow Models
arxiv-2412-08175.creator: Huminhao Zhu, Fangyikang Wang, Tianyu Ding, Qing Qu, Zhihui Zhu
arxiv-2412-08175.description: Abstract Training with synthetic data is becoming increasingly inevitable as synthetic content proliferates across the web, driven by the remarkable performance of recent deep generative models. This reliance on synthetic data can also be intentional, as seen in Rectified Flow models, whose Reflow method iteratively uses self-generated data to straighten the flow and improve sampling efficiency.

arxiv-2512-11125.title: Design and Experimental Validation of Closed-Form CBF-Based Safe Control for Stewart Platform Under Multiple Constraints PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2512-11125.creator: Benedictus C. G. Cinun, Tua A. Tamba, Immanuel R. Santjoko, Xiaofeng Wang, Michael A. Gunarso, Bin Hu
arxiv-2512-11125.description: Abstract This letter presents a closed-form solution of Control Barrier Function (CBF) framework for enforcing safety constraints on a Stewart robotic platform. The proposed method simultaneously handles multiple position and velocity constraints through an explicit closed-form control law, eliminating the need to solve a Quadratic Program (QP) at every control step and enabling efficient real-time implementation.

pmc-11350104.creator: Vinicius Tadeu Ramos da Silva Grillo, Matheus Bertanha, Lenize da Silva Rodrigues, Marcelo Andrade de Lima, Pedro Luciano Mellucci Filho, Rafael Rahal Guaragna Machado, Edson Luiz Durigon, Nathália Dias Sertorio, Marjorie de Assis Golim, Andrei Moroz, Aline Márcia Marques Braz, Leonardo Nazário de M
pmc-11350104.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To evaluate the safety and the potential antiviral treatment of inhaled enriched heparin in patients with COVID-19. The specific objectives were to investigate the anticoagulation profile, antiviral and anti-inflammatory effects, and respiratory evolution of inhaled enriched heparin. We conducted a randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled Phase I/II clinical trial in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 receiving inhalation of enriched heparin or saline (placebo) every 4 h for 7 days.

pmc-11357790.title: Mechanism of action of FoxiangSan in diabetic gastroparesis: Gut microbiota and cAMP/PKA pathway
pmc-11357790.creator: Jukai Huang, Yaling Song, Shuli Cheng, Xiaohui Yang
pmc-11357790.description: Diabetic gastroparesis, a common complication of type 2 diabetes (T2DM), presents a significant treatment challenge. FoxiangSan is emerging as a potential therapy. FoxiangSan is a traditional Chinese medicine formula with the potential for treating diabetic gastroparesis by modulating gut microbiota and cAMP/PKA signaling pathways.

pmc-11504891.title: Insights into CSF-1R Expression in the Tumor Microenvironment
pmc-11504891.creator: Caterina Tomassetti, Gaia Insinga, Francesca Gimigliano, Andrea Morrione, Antonio Giordano, Emanuele Giurisato, Amirata Saei Dibavar, Akira Hara
pmc-11504891.description: The colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF-1R) plays a pivotal role in orchestrating cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Although the CSF-1R has been extensively studied in myeloid cells, the expression of this receptor and its emerging role in other cell types in the TME need to be further analyzed.

We evaluated the effectiveness of original monovalent and bivalent (ancestral strain and Omicron BA.4/5) COVID‐19 vaccination against COVID‐19‐associated hospitalization and severe in‐hospital outcomes.

pmc-11611881.title: Level of health laboratory service quality, service interruptions, and its predictors in public hospitals in Harar town, eastern Ethiopia
pmc-11611881.creator: Dire Zakir, Getachaw Kabew Mekonnen, Belay Negash, Dadi Marami
pmc-11611881.description: BackgroundQuality laboratory services are key in the healthcare system for successful diagnosis and patient care. Uninterrupted laboratory services are needed to meet the needs of all patients and clinical personnel, but studies in developing nations revealed that most clinicians were dissatisfied due to the lack of quality laboratory services and frequent interruptions.

pmc-12516381.title: Comparative effectiveness of lumbar interbody fusion techniques in adult scoliosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of postoperative alignment and disability outcomes
pmc-12516381.creator: Zachary Taylor, David Gomez, Blake Nygaard, Spencer Newell, Zak Sabetta, Jacob Ayers, Kyle Zappi, Neel H. Mehta, Ian Hong, Jibran Khan, John Shin
pmc-12516381.description: BackgroundAdult scoliosis, marked by degenerative and pathological changes in the spinal column, is a growing health concern, particularly among the elderly, often leading to chronic pain and functional limitations. Initial management typically includes conservative approaches such as physical therapy; however, persistent symptoms frequently necessitate surgical intervention.

pmc-13020269.title: Predicting adverse prognostic outcomes in hospitalized breast cancer patients: development and validation of a risk model
pmc-13020269.creator: Liya Ma, Endi Cai, Zhiyuan Zhou, Mengchun Gong, Chen Li
pmc-13020269.description: BackgroundBreast cancer prognosis is influenced by diverse clinical factors, necessitating advanced predictive tools for personalized treatment. This study developed machine learning models to predict adverse outcomes in breast cancer patients using comprehensive clinical data.MethodsWe analyzed data from 4,242 patients (3,836 with stable progression and 406 with adverse outcomes) at a single institution.

pmc-13087244.title: Lipid homeostasis plays a critical role in inherited and acquired retinal diseases
pmc-13087244.creator: Anwesha Bhattacharyya, Vineet Choudhary
pmc-13087244.description: The photoreceptor layer of the retina converts light stimuli into electrical signals and transmits them to the visual cortex for image processing. Photoreceptor cells rely on a constant supply of nutrients, including lipids, to replenish their high demand of membrane remodelling.

pmc-13363676.title: Comparative Analysis of the Association of Biomarkers of Endothelial Dysfunction and Systemic Inflammation in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease with the Presence/Absence of Personality Type D

pmc-13526318.title: Derivation of functional retinal endothelial cells from human pluripotent stem cells for therapeutics and modelling
pmc-13526318.creator: Ying-Yu Lin, Parker Esswein, Lucas Ramirez, Emily Warren, Julian Nicenboim, Sharon Gerecht
pmc-13526318.description: Retinal microvascular diseases involve a compromised inner blood–retina barrier (iBRB), which remains poorly understood. A renewable source of human iBRB endothelium is thus vital for advancing eye research and treatment development. Here we differentiated human induced pluripotent stem cells into retinal endothelial cells (iRECs) via the Wnt–β-catenin pathway, namely Norrin–Frizzled4 signalling.
